baselineAudit.notes: Static triage only. 100/244 items in the third rewrite tranche are classified for substantive revision and qualified educator review; no clinical approval or content changes were recorded.

commonFindings: All 20 are single-response items built from a repeated generic reassessment stem and four reusable answer/rationale families; the task does not distinguish the named endocrine or renal learning objective.
Named endocrine disorders generally lack defining history, vital-sign patterns, laboratory values, diagnostic criteria or treatment timeline.
Renal/dialysis items omit key context such as baseline renal function, dialysis session/ultrafiltration, peritoneal-dialysis exchanges or vascular-access history.
Unrelated acute abnormalities (hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia, severe hyponatremia/seizure, INR/hematuria, bleeding, respiratory acidosis) compete with or contradict the named topic.
Several demographics/context details are clinically unsupported (e.g., newborn insulin-pump interruption; pediatric post-thyroidectomy/AV fistula contexts without surgical/access history).
